canonical_name: HumanEval (OpenAI, 'Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code')
metric: pass@1 (functional correctness on hidden unit tests; unbiased pass@k estimator)
ab_system: Reflexion (GPT-4 with self-reflection and self-generated unit tests)
ab_mode: pass@1 (one final submission after internal iterations; code executed only against the agent's own generated tests)
ab_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366v2 (v2 2023-05-21: 'Reflexion achieves a 91% pass@1 accuracy on the HumanEval coding benchmark, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art GPT-4 that achieves 80%'; v1 2023-03-20 had no coding results)
strict_system: GPT-4-Turbo (gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09), EvalPlus leaderboard run (base HumanEval tests)
score_at_release_system: Codex-S 12B, single sample (paper: 'Codex-S ... solves 37.7% of the problems'); Codex-12B 28.8; mean-logp reranking of 100 samples 44.5
lineage: HumanEval (2021-07) -> HumanEval+ / EvalPlus (arXiv 2305.01210, 2023-05; ~80x more tests), multilingual MultiPL-E (2022), HumanEval-X (2023), HumanEval-Mul (DeepSeek-V3 reports). Labs later moved to LiveCodeBench / SWE-bench.
best_by_cutoff: Single model, independent: 96.3 o1-preview and o1-mini (EvalPlus leaderboard, added 2024-11-10; leaderboard last updated 2024-12-26). Self-report: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (new) 93.7 (2024-10-22 model card). Agent scaffolds claim higher (e.g., LATS 92.7 pass@1 with GPT-4 in arXiv 2310.04406 v1, 2023-10).
notes: Judgement call on tools: HumanEval has no explicit no-tools protocol and the codebook counts scaffolds, so the Reflexion agent (runs code only against its own self-written tests; hidden tests used once) counts for AB. If execution-feedback agents were excluded as tool-assisted, AB would move to 2024-04 (EvalPlus GPT-4-Turbo-2024-04-09 90.2, independent), with lab self-reports GPT-4o 90.2 (2024-05-13 simple-evals) and Claude 3.5 Sonnet 92.0 (2024-06-20). EvalPlus history: GPT-4 (May 2023) 88.4 was the top single model before 2024-04. No C event: OpenAI's simple-evals README (2025-07) deprecates the repo's result tables in general; its 'saturated' footnote [^5] is attached to MGSM/DROP, not HumanEval. No E event coded: EvalPlus showed insufficient tests (pass@k drops), and contamination concerns exist, but no audit with >=20% defective items followed by a lab stopping, and no contamination study covering most frontier models was found. Several raw_names (human-evaluation win rates for Grok voice/video, Flan-PaLM human eval, DeepSeek-VL) are parsing noise, not HumanEval.

canonical_name: LAB-Bench: Measuring Capabilities of Language Models for Biology Research (FutureHouse)
metric: per-category accuracy (correct/all), precision (correct/attempted) and coverage over 8 categories (LitQA2, SuppQA, FigQA, TableQA, DbQA, ProtocolQA, SeqQA, CloningScenarios); no aggregate score is defined
human_baseline: per category, PhD-level biologists (with internet and sequence tools): e.g., accuracy LitQA2 70, SuppQA 85, FigQA 77, TableQA 84 (82% coverage); others not extracted
threshold: 90 (per category; most category baselines <85%; no aggregate to apply it to)
c_source: https://edisonscientific.com/news/labbench2-an-improved-benchmark (2026-02-05; Edison Scientific = LAB-Bench creators Laurent, Narayanan, White, Rodriques per https://arxiv.org/html/2604.09554v2)
c_quote: "Despite some LAB-Bench subsets still being difficult, we have seen saturation or superhuman performance on others." LABBench2 built 'to make it more difficult than the original'; paper: 'multiple examples of near saturation or superhuman performance on LAB-Bench subcategories'
score_at_release: category-level only: TableQA 83 (accuracy), FigQA 46, ProtocolQA ~60 precision, SeqQA ~50 precision
score_at_release_system: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (best model in most categories at release, per arXiv v1)
n_items: 2,457 (LitQA2 248, SuppQA 102, FigQA 226, TableQA 305, DbQA 650, ProtocolQA 135, SeqQA 750, CloningScenarios 41); ~80% public / 20% held out
lineage: LAB-Bench (2024-07) -> LABBench2 (Edison Scientific, announced 2026-02-05; arXiv 2604.09554, ~1,900 tasks, 'a continuation of LAB-Bench ... in more realistic contexts'). LABBench2 reported by OpenAI (GPT-Rosalind 2026-04-16) and Google (Gemini 3.7/3.8 Flash, 2026-08/09); separate unit.
best_by_cutoff: Sub-metrics only (self-reports per lab_reports): FigQA 88.9 no tools / 90.7 with tools, Claude Mythos 5 / Fable 5 (2026-06-09); xAI 'LAB-Bench practical MCQ accuracy' Grok 4.6 80.7 (2026-08-12). LABBench2 (successor): Gemini 3.8 Flash 86.2 (2026-09-02)
notes: Hard call: LAB-Bench has no aggregate metric and labs report different subsets (Anthropic FigQA/ProtocolQA/SeqQA/Cloning; xAI an MCQ aggregate; OpenAI ProtocolQA), so AB/B could not be applied to the unit; no per-category crossing dates were coded. Primary event is C: the creators (now at Edison Scientific/FutureHouse) cite saturation or superhuman performance on some LAB-Bench subsets as the reason for the harder LABBench2. The statement is partial (some subsets 'still being difficult'). Human baselines were measured with internet and tools, while model evals were mostly tool-free; Anthropic's FigQA 'with tools' numbers would not count under a no-tools reading. If FigQA alone were the unit: B threshold 90 reached only with tools (90.7, 2026-06).
